title: The L1 intake slice in rwb-agent: the service login, the policy values and keys of the L1 gate, the case-decision proposal path, the name of the acceptance event, the route path and the freshness read are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 15; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7 (FEAT-AGT-07) and A2.6; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-111), T3.2, T5.2, T5.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2 (API-P10-010, API-P10-011); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14, 15, 16, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 13 and 28; Ownership Map v1 (eight agent tables owner P10, P10 operations, EV-28 owner P10, reference data owner P3, decision_log_entry owner P7); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5, §R5.7 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths X9 to X12; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: Seven values the app slice of this key needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The per-service login of rwb-agent is required by DP-02 and no source names it. (2) The L1 gate is built from policy data - the autonomy mode, the segment, the segment threshold and the confidence floor - but no source names the parameter keys or the operation that carries them, and the legacy story held them in a loader schema beside the code. (3) The legacy read of the case facts, the owner check and the scope was an in-process call, and no source names the path of the case-decision proposal operation of rwb-case to which the owner's verdict is offered. (4) The event catalogue names only AgentRunCompleted on rwb.agent.events.v1, so the name and payload of the L1 acceptance event are a realignment decision. (5) The name and path of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations are not named. (6) The business date of AC9 is the freshness of the ACE load, and no source names the operation shape beyond the GET /freshness of Arch v5 slide 15. (7) The migration numbering after the baseline V10_001__agent_runtime.sql is unstated, although the legacy story names V10_008__agent_feedback.sql for its own table.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 3 ('RWB-E1-061 is done and policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with mode L1 is approved by RW-RISK, valid from 2027-01-25') and section 12 (the two operations on the legacy monolith base, the event list EV-01, EV-28 and EV-08); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 lists API-P10-010 and API-P10-011 only and no start, no eligibility and no case-decision operation; Architecture v5 slide 43 row 28 names AgentRunCompleted as the only event of rwb.agent.events.v1; slide 15 names GET /freshness for rwb-source-data; slide 41 gives the base /api/recovery/<name>/v1 behind gateway-bff; Ownership Map v1 has no row for an eligibility operation, a case-decision proposal or a route.
owner_role: Solution architect with the tech lead of rwb-agent and the owner of rwb-case
proposed: Name the service login from the platform at build time, keep the gate values as policy data read at run time, fix the case-decision proposal path with the rwb-case owner, declare rwb.agent.AgentFeedbackRecorded.v1 under the naming rule, treat the route as a one-hop pass-through, read the business date through the freshness read and keep the legacy migration number V10_008__agent_feedback.sql.

title: The L1 intake contract slice: the member types beyond the names, the eligibility answer members, the record member types, the acceptance event payload and the route path are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 12 (the two operations, the AgentOutput and AgentFeedbackRequest members, the decision log mapping and the events) and section 7; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (decision_log_entry owner P7, reference data owner P3, P10 operations); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths X3 to X8; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1, 12.2, 12.3 and 12.8; 15 Screens and states
description: Six elements of the contract are open in the sources. (1) The legacy answer names its members without a schema: the type and length of summary, the nested type of each gap reason and the form of dataAsOf and recordedAt beyond a date are not given. (2) The segment eligibility answer is new in the target, because the legacy mode came from a loader table, so its members and its SERVED and SHADOW outcomes have no source. (3) The record mapping is named by the legacy story but the type and length of its inputs reference and of its recommendation member are given by no source, and the record shape belongs to the library and to rwb-decision. (4) The event catalogue names one event on rwb.agent.events.v1, so the payload of the L1 acceptance event is taken from the agent_feedback fields of TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and not from a published schema. (5) The case-decision proposal operation of rwb-case has no path in any source. (6) The route name and path in front of the two operations are not named. The contract fixes the member names and leaves the types to the review with their owners.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 12 ('AgentOutput (runId, agent, agentVersion, mode "L1", status, summary, gaps[{gapType, reason}], confidence, dataAsOf, feedback)' and 'AgentFeedbackRequest (itemKey, default "SUMMARY" ... reason ... at most 1,000 characters)'); TSD P10 v2 T3.1 gives the agent_feedback and agent_run field types and T-A.2 gives purpose, errors and authorization only; Arch v5 slide 43 row 28 names AgentRunCompleted as the only agent event; no source names a route or a case-decision proposal path.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owner of rwb-decision
proposed: Fix the member names once, leave the member types to the contract review with their owners, declare the eligibility answer with SERVED and SHADOW, map the record to the ledger members of the library, name the acceptance event under §R4 and open the route path with the edge owner.

title: The L1 intake deployment: the login name, the route path, the topology, the alert thresholds, the topic partitions and retention, the dashboard retention and the consumer groups of the agent topic are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 5 and 12; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T5.3 and T7 (NFR-009, NFR-010); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 20, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 28; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5, §R7.2 and §R9; Ownership Map v1
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths X1 to X12; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.2, 12.4 and 12.6; 13 Solution plan
description: The deployment story needs values that no source carries, and it must not invent one: the cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and exact probe timings; the host, the SKU and the budget of the release; the exact path of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations; the login name of the rwb-agent service; the partition count, replication factor and retention of rwb.agent.events.v1 and of its retry and .dlt topics, and the relay interval of the outbox; the thresholds of the dashboard series and of the six alert rules, including the floor of the acceptance rate, the ceiling of the override rate, the window of the backlog rule and the retention of the series; and the identity of the consumer groups of rwb.agent.events.v1, which belong to rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation and rwb-reporting and are created by their own releases. The legacy story fixes the policy version, the case identifiers, the rates 0.8000 and 0.1500 and the message IDs, and those are kept as they are; every other number is a value of the environment.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 3 ('policy "INTAKE" version "P2" ... valid from 2027-01-25'), section 4 (the panel path) and section 12 (the two operations); Architecture v5 slide 43 row 28 lists the consumers of AgentRunCompleted but names no group; slide 16 gives the queue rwb-agent and the topic rwb.agent.events.v1 without a partition or a retention; TSD P10 v2 T7 gives NFR-009 under 2 seconds and NFR-010 under 60 seconds with no measurement point or alert threshold; no source names a route or a login.
owner_role: DevOps team with the platform event owner, the platform observability owner and the ACE database team
proposed: Fix the names of every value in the chart and the rule that none is hard-coded, hold the thresholds and the retention as reviewed values per environment, name the login through a secret reference, and verify the consume rights of the four consumers while their groups stay with their own releases.
